recipes.name: Blue Cheese, Spinach Meat Loaf Muffins

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a large muffin pan with cooking spray.
Combine ground beef, blue cheese, onion, bread crumbs, spinach, eggs, and Worcestershire sauce in a large bowl until well blended. Divide meat mixture evenly into the prepared muffin pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, about 30 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Blue Cheese, Spinach Meat Loaf Muffins
raw_recipe.description: Using a large muffin pan allows the mini meat loaves to cook faster and makes portion sizing easier, plus your kids won't know you hid some veggies in there too!

review.reviewBody: made them lastnight for the picky eaters in my home....& WOW they both loved it!!! My 12yr old niece hates everything, and she asked for more! I used turkey instead of beef. Thank You!

I had blue cheese (St.Agur) to use up, and in my search for what to do with this wonderful cheese I found this recipe. Having read previous comments from the others stating that adults and children both liked the blue cheese meatloaf, I thought I would try and slip this recipe by my blue cheese detesting husband. Wow did this work! The faint taste of the blue cheese was there, but undetected by his lordship. The meatloaf muffins were so flavourful and moist that I will definitely make them again. My changes included panko versus Italian bread crumbs, double the cheese and spinach, and the addition of a diced roasted red pepper then topped in the last 10 minutes of baking with an apple jelly barbecue sauce. Delish!!!
loved iy. made it a few times but I added 1/4 cup sweet Baby rays bbq sauce as well as 1/4 cup bacon (bacon makes everything better) and glazed top w the bbq. was awesome.

it was very good the first time, but I use turkey not beef. the second time, I cooked two strips of bacon and chopped it up and add to mixture, also add 2 tablespoons of ketchup also. didn't use muffin tin, but pan for making small loafs of bread. makes 8 small loafs.

This is without a doubt the best meatloaf recipe I've ever made. I make mine with ground turkey or ground beef.I like to make a double or triple batch and freeze them up in tinfoil muffin tins. I pull them out and thaw them or bake from frozen. My family loves this recipe and it is so delicious. This recipe is so adaptable...you can throw in grated carrot,finely chopped mushroom, whatever you want. I top some of them with a ketchup, brown sugar, mustard topping before baking. Love,love,love!

Great! Sauted onion with a clove of garlic before adding to meat mixture. Added pepper and used extra spinach. Used onion hamburger buns for bread crumbs. So moist and delish. Even though I used lean ground beef there was a lot of oil sitting in pan when pulled from oven. Key is to remove meat from tin (using tongs) immediately to drain on paper towel.

Interesting flavor, easy prep. I did increase spinach as suggested by others and enjoyed the taste. I served it with Roasted rosemary butternut squash from this site and it was a perfect accompaniment. Will make this again.

Can't believe I haven't left a review before, but I've been using this recipe for years and it's absolutely delicious! I finally convinced my picky daughter to try it after many times and now she's convinced too. I always add shredded carrots, more onion, some extra spices, and lately I've been doing 1 lb ground beef and 1 lb ground turkey (health and cost benefits) and it's just as good as ever. This is one of those recipes where I will eat the leftovers cold for breakfast, it's that amazing. Thank you to the creator for many years of happy meatloaf muffins!

This was AMAZING! I was looking for some "easy protein" and stumbled across this gem. They taste great hot or cold. I also prepped some steamed vegetables along with some quinoa and rice. All week I had these amazing lunches that were ready in about 1:20 in the microwave. Yum! I did make some changes , but only because I didn't have some of the ingredients on hand. I substituted Kale for Spinach and "Coaches Oats" oatmeal for the bread crumbs. I also threw in some fresh basil simply because I had it and wanted to use it before it went bad. My wife loved them; however, the bleu cheese didn't appeal to the kids (which is fine by me). Oh, I also used grass-fed beef. I ended up making 24 of these "muffins" and I did a rough calculation and I think it works out to about 140 calories each, and each one packed a tasty 11.4 grams of protein. I'll be making these every week from now on! Awesome recipe!

I make this a lot, and love it every time. I have done it with all turkey, half and half or all beef, and it is always yummy. I have also done it in both the muffin tins or as a loaf (usually about 45 min). Substituting cheeses has been fun (feta, Gorgonzola) and adding peas or other veggies has also worked. To make it glutton free for my husband, I used crushed chex mix instead of bread crumbs and it tasted wonderful. Highly recommend and super easy.

What a fantastic, sophisticated play on meat loaf! The blue cheese creates a heavenly bite while the spinach lends an earthy tone...a sophisticated flare yet an old home satisfaction. The only thing I did differently was increase the blue cheese, onion and spinach to one cup each... also used 85% lean beef... very little run off, if at all. absolutely delicious. Pared with a petit Syrah.
Tasty but not outstanding. Lacked any sort of zing. I think it is a good base recipe, but haven't figured out what to add to make me want to make it again.
Much better than I expected! Honestly the best meat loaf i've ever made. The flavors meld perfectly together and the blue cheese is much less sharp than I would've expected.
Delicious cooked this in our BBQ pellet and it was so so good
We loved it! Very tasty and nice portions. We will definitely make it again.
Husband loved flavor, though next time (and all future meatloaf meals) he wants an actual loaf.
Super yummy
I used onion powder instead of onions as I am allergic to cooked onions and I only had plain bread crumbs so I added some Italian spices.

This was a nice change, but my family definitely prefers a sweeter, glazed meatloaf. I enjoyed the blue cheese and spinach combination, but the kids definitely weren’t having it. The flavor was a little too grown up for them. I will probably freeze the remaining muffins and take them for lunch until they’re gone.

My blue cheese hating husband didn't believe there was blue cheese in these! these were super easy to make and everyone in the family loved them. I used dehydrated onions since typical onions give me tummy issues and I added salt and pepper. Those were the only modifications I made and they turned out great!
